sections.h2: Who sends, collects and enforces a Franklin County tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work. The appraiser values the parcel, the tax collector bills it, and the clerk of court conducts any tax deed auction. The county commission, school board and the cities of Apalachicola and Carrabelle set the rates.

Franklin County lies in the northwestern Panhandle, roughly 80 miles southwest of Tallahassee, across 545 square miles and 348,800 acres. The county site cites more than 11,000 residents and a founding year of 1832. Outside the two cities, the commission serves as the local government.

  • Property appraiser: keeps the roll, takes exemption filings, mails TRIM notices in August. Per its home page, the office neither sets rates nor collects tax.
  • Tax collector: 33 Market Street, Suite 202, Apalachicola; (850) 653-9323. Prints bills, accepts payment, sells certificates.
  • Clerk: holds the courthouse auction of tax deeds and records your deed when you sell.

sections.h2: What are the Franklin County property tax dates?
sections.html:
The property appraiser's calendar starts on January 1, when exemption and agricultural classification filing opens, and the application deadline is March 1. Tangible personal property returns are due April 1. TRIM notices go out in August, and the office says plainly that the notice is not a bill.

The tax collector says statements are mailed on or before November 1. Payment in November earns a 4 percent discount, December 3 percent, January 2 percent and February 1 percent. After that the bill is at face value through March, and the tax becomes delinquent on April 1.

sections.h2: What millage rates does the Franklin County tax collector list?
sections.html:
The tax collector's millage page lists a table headed "Franklin 2025 millage", broken out by taxing unit and printed in decimal form. Ask the tax collector for the current-year table before you plan around these figures, since the published table carries the 2025 label.

  • County: .00504590
  • School, required local effort: .00194400
  • School, discretionary: .00224800
  • Northwest Florida Water Management: .00002070
  • Carrabelle: .00750000
  • Apalachicola: .00834570
  • Dog Island: .00400000
  • Eastpoint district: .00375000
  • Alligator Point: .00123040

The county, school and water lines apply across the county. The city and district lines apply only where the parcel sits, so a house in Apalachicola carries a different total from one on Dog Island or at Alligator Point. The parcel search on the tax collector's site shows the exact lines for your address, and non-ad valorem assessments appear on the same bill.

sections.h2: What reduces a Franklin County bill?
sections.html:
A permanent residence qualifies for the Florida homestead exemption of up to $50,000 of value, described in the Department of Revenue guide. The filing window runs January 1 to March 1 at the appraiser's office, and renting the house out ends eligibility.

Once a homestead is in place, a statutory cap restrains how fast its assessed value can rise. A sale wipes out that cushion for the next owner, so the buyer's first Franklin County bill may look much larger than yours did.

sections.h2: Can the bill be paid in pieces in Franklin County?
sections.html: The state permits quarterly prepayment under s. 197.222 if you apply to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year, and low-income homestead owners can defer part of the tax with Form DR-570 by March 31. Both come from the state taxpayer page. Whether either route helps depends on your income and timing, so phone the collector at (850) 653-9323 before the dates pass. Mortgage escrow lenders normally settle the bill themselves.

sections.h2: What happens when Franklin County tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Real estate tax turns delinquent on April 1, and a 3 percent penalty is added. The collector advertises unpaid parcels in the local paper once a week for three weeks in May, and the cost is added to the bill. Unpaid personal property carries 1.5 percent per month instead.

On or before June 1 the collector sells tax certificates online. Bidding opens at 18 percent and goes down, and the lowest bid wins. A certificate is a lien, not a sale of your house. The collector page says a certificate holder who is not paid within 22 months can lose the owner the property at a tax deed sale, and the glossary says the holder may apply for a deed two years after April 1 of the year of issue.

Homestead parcels with under $250 owed are not sold to the public. They go to the county and carry 18 percent interest per year until the balance passes $250.

sections.h2: How does a Franklin County tax deed sale work?
sections.html:
The clerk's office runs the sale. Franklin County sales, when scheduled, are generally held on the first Monday of the month at 11:00 AM inside the main courthouse at 33 Market Street, Apalachicola, and the clerk tells people to call to verify before attending. Notice runs in the Apalachicola Times once a week for four weeks.

  • You can redeem by paying the tax collector before the sale, or before the clerk receives the winning bidder's full payment.
  • For homestead property, the opening bid adds half of the latest assessed value to the taxes, interest and fees.
  • The winning bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is greater, and pays the balance within 24 hours.
  • Documentary stamps of $.70 per $100 of the bid and recording fees are due from the bidder.
  • Some government liens survive the deed, and every property is sold as is.

sections.h2: What does a Franklin County seller do about taxes at closing?
sections.html:
An unpaid balance is a lien the buyer's title company will insist on clearing. The closing agent can send the payoff to the tax collector out of the seller's proceeds. Request a figure good through the closing day, since a bill past April 1 grows by a 3 percent penalty and newspaper advertising.

The state also taxes the deed itself. Documentary stamps run 70 cents on each $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, and every party to the document is liable, according to the Department of Revenue. The clerk takes the payment at recording.

faqs.q: Which month is the cheapest to pay in Franklin County?
faqs.a: November. The tax collector prints a 4 percent discount for November, 3 percent for December, 2 percent for January and 1 percent for February.

faqs.q: Does the appraiser or the collector set my rate?
faqs.a: Neither. Per the appraiser's home page, that office does not set rates, and the tax collector's millage page says the county commission, school board and each city or district do.

faqs.q: Is a house with a tax certificate on it still sellable?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays the redemption to the tax collector, which then repays the certificate holder. Ask (850) 653-9323 for the redemption total.

faqs.q: When is the Franklin County exemption filing cutoff?
faqs.a: March 1. Filing opens January 1, and the appraiser notes the home must be your permanent residence.

faqs.q: How fast can a tax deed auction happen?
faqs.a: Slowly. A certificate holder waits two years after April 1 of the issue year to apply, and you can redeem up to the point the clerk receives the winning bidder's full payment.
